analysis:
Examined the added ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts+Release.swift and the modified ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts.swift (patch plus base text). The change moves the schema from cluster_runtime_v1 to v2 and adds per-model pair_serving_grant and parity_qualifications, release-lane computation of facts (`release`, `releaseModels`, `candidates`), and a strict canonical parser (`init(canonical:)`). The parser is bounded to 64 KiB, checks exact key sets, rejects duplicate keys with a custom scanner, requires tensor_parallel_shares to be null, and checks derived ID lengths.

Security-relevant observations:
- The facts are produced offline by the release CLI and worker from the signed app. Digests come from the existing DistributedInstalledFiles.digest path, and the worker is pinned to its own computed SHA via --expected-executable-sha256. The worker is run through DistributedCapabilityProbe with a deadline, and the described capability must match the runtime binary hash, artifact hash and absence of private images. Model grants for declared models come from compiled-in ClusterPublicModels.declared, and others from bundled records. So the claims are build-attested rather than caller-supplied.
- Catalog input is bounded: catalog.json is limited to 4096 bytes with an exact key set, ID match, and modality count and length checks. layerCount reads config.json with a bounded size. Paths go through realpath canonicalization. Candidate folders are listed without following dot-prefixed entries; per-file realpath resolves symlinks, but the inputs are release-lane operator-controlled and not attacker input in the provider threat model.
- validate() enforces non-zero hex digests, sorted unique models, grant family rules, and parity checks (schedule 1 or 2, member counts, cuts, not diverged and promotable, RFC 3339 time, token bounds, no repeated placement). The facts approve nothing by themselves. Enforcement of the grants and qualifications, and any widening of serving authority (T-052, T-054, T-053), lies in coordinator and platform code outside the supplied evidence.
- The new constants (evidenceSHA256, qualifiedAt) and the media-serving policy come from unseen files (ClusterPublicModels, ClusterModelFeaturePolicy, ClusterPairServingGrants). Their correctness is not verified here.

No concrete regression was identified. Remaining integration questions: how the coordinator consumes v2 facts, and whether v1 consumers fail closed on the schema change. Neither is evidenced here.
